findings.title: Duplicate guest emails in a single request are inserted
findings.body: The handler filters incoming guests only against existing booking attendees and does not de-duplicate the request payload. Because the schema also does not enforce uniqueness, a request containing the same email twice will pass validation and create multiple attendee rows for the same booking, or cause a database constraint failure if one exists. This can corrupt attendee data and send duplicate emails. De-duplicate and normalize guests before creating attendees.

findings.title: Email comparisons are case-sensitive and blacklist can be bypassed
findings.body: BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS is lowercased, but incoming guest emails are not normalized before comparison. An uppercase variant of a blacklisted address can bypass the block. Existing attendee emails are also compared with strict equality, so User@example.com and user@example.com are treated as different addresses, allowing duplicate attendees. Normalize email addresses before comparing them to attendees, the blacklist, and before storing them.

findings.title: No upper bound on number of guest emails
findings.body: The guests array is unbounded. An authenticated user can submit a very large list of email addresses, causing a large createMany write and potentially triggering mass notification emails. Add a reasonable maximum length to the guests array.

findings.title: Team permission check uses && instead of ||
findings.body: isTeamAdminOrOwner is computed by combining isTeamAdmin and isTeamOwner with &&, meaning a user must pass both checks. The name and intended behavior imply admin or owner should be allowed. As written, team admins who are not owners can be incorrectly rejected. Use a logical OR or a single role check that matches the intended permission.

findings.title: Emails are sent using the unfiltered guest list
findings.body: sendAddGuestsEmails receives the original guests input instead of uniqueGuests, the list of guests actually inserted. If the request includes an existing attendee email, that attendee may be treated as a new guest and receive a normal scheduled email instead of the add-guests notification. Duplicate inputs can also cause duplicate emails. Pass the normalized, de-duplicated list of newly added guests.

findings.title: No booking status or time validation
findings.body: The handler only checks whether the caller can access the booking; it does not check whether the booking is cancelled, rejected, or already in the past. The API can therefore add guests to bookings that should no longer be modified, sending emails and updating calendar events unnecessarily. Validate booking status and timing before allowing guests to be added.

findings.title: Calendar update uses requester's credentials instead of booking owner's
findings.body: EventManager is constructed with credentials for ctx.user, while the booking query already loads booking.user.credentials. If a team admin or attendee adds guests, the request may use credentials that do not own the target calendar event, causing calendar updates to fail or update the wrong calendar. Use the appropriate booking owner/host credentials for the calendar update.

findings.title: Add-guests emails ignore email-disable settings
findings.body: sendAddGuestsEmails always sends organizer, team-member, and attendee emails and does not accept or honor event-type email disabling metadata. Similar email flows check eventTypeDisableHostEmail and eventTypeDisableAttendeeEmail. Event types configured to suppress standard emails will still send add-guest emails.

findings.title: Organizer lookup throws for bookings without a user
findings.body: The organizer lookup uses booking.userId || 0 with findFirstOrThrow. If a booking has no associated user, this queries user id 0 and throws an unhandled Prisma error instead of returning a controlled TRPC error. Handle missing booking owners explicitly.

findings.title: Invalid-email error state is not reset
findings.body: isInvalidEmail is set to true when client-side validation fails, but it is not cleared when the user edits the email list or when the mutation succeeds. After a failed validation followed by a successful submission, reopening the dialog can show a stale invalid-email error. Reset the flag on input changes and on successful submission.

findings.title: Error fallback toast is unreachable
findings.body: The error message is created with a template string, so it is always truthy even when err.data?.code or the translated message is missing. The fallback t("unable_to_add_guests") therefore never runs, and users may see messages like undefined: ... Build the message conditionally before showing the toast.

findings.title: Hardcoded English tooltip
findings.body: The remove-email tooltip uses the hardcoded string Remove email instead of a translated locale key. Non-English users will see untranslated text. Use the locale system for this label.

findings.title: Unsafe access to first attendee
findings.body: The organizer email subject accesses this.calEvent.attendees[0].name without checking that attendees exist. If the attendees array is empty, email rendering throws. Use optional chaining or a fallback value.
